note: FNS 1070.2 requires income proration for members ineligible due to SSN disqualifications, comparable disqualifications, child support disqualifications, ineligible ABAWDs, and ineligible non-citizens. The OLG covers some but not all of these categories. For ABAWD-disqualified members, the 'ABAWD Work Rules Disqualification Process' page provides a detailed 5-step proration methodology with a worked example (divide income by total HH members, multiply by eligible members, reduce HH size). For ineligible non-citizens, the 'Calculation Rules and Attribution of Income for Mixed Noncitizen Households' page describes a different 'combination calculation' method per 106 CMR 364.600(C), and the 'Nonimmigrants' page states that nonimmigrant/undetermined/undocumented noncitizen income is 'considered available to any remaining household member(s).' The 'Nonhousehold Members' page establishes the general principle that disqualified individuals' income IS counted (unlike other nonhousehold members whose income is excluded), but does not describe the proration methodology generically. Missing from the OLG: (1) no income proration procedure for SSN-disqualified members specifically, (2) no income proration procedure for child support disqualification, (3) no income proration procedure for comparable disqualifications (IPV, fleeing felon, trafficking). The ABAWD proration page likely reflects the same methodology BEACON applies to other disqualification types, but this is not documented in the OLG for those categories. A worker encountering a non-ABAWD disqualified member with income would not find explicit written guidance on how to prorate that income.
